Working Concept · Decision Deck

One idea.
Multiple ways to build it.

The strategy is REAL. The format, seating, ticket model, production level, and final budget are decisions. This proposal shows the tradeoffs before we lock the event.

The Premise

Rather than ask talented agents to learn about The Young Team, we build a room talented agents consider worth entering.

REAL is intentionally not a recruiting event, a CE class, or a traditional conference. The Young Team creates and hosts a room productive agents find worth entering on its own merit — and the relationship develops naturally from there. Built as a repeatable annual property, not a one-time event.

What REAL Means

Not an acronym. A standard.

REAL CONVERSATIONS
REAL NUMBERS
REAL PROBLEMS
REAL PEOPLE DOING THE WORK
REAL ANSWERS — EVEN WHEN THE ANSWER IS "IT DIDN'T WORK"

A natural extension of the Young Team brand — bold, professional, approachable. Not a separate conference brand that happens to carry the logo.

Strategic Objectives

Five returns

01

Recruiting

Create warm relationships with productive agents before any recruiting conversation begins. Not five hires on December 2 — a warmer recruiting environment that compounds.

02

Market Position

Position Josh and The Young Team as conveners of the valuable real estate conversations in Northeast Ohio.

03

Relationships

Strengthen connections with agents, leaders, vendors, sponsors, and potential future recruits.

04

Content

Capture months of professional recruiting and thought-leadership content from a single afternoon.

05

Market Intelligence

Hear directly from productive agents on lead gen, AI, technology, brokerage pain points, and business models.

Seating & Room Plan

Same Oak Room. Two different experiences.

Use Sapphire Creek's existing screen, projector, and microphone in either version. Keep physical branding minimal. No giant banners, no LED wall, and no stage unless we decide the visual separation is worth the additional spend.

Conference Casual
Seated program + flexible perimeter
Concept Mockup · Conference Casual

Rows of upholstered chairs facing a simple 3–4 chair conversation area, with a few high-tops around the perimeter for arrival and networking.

Executive Dinner
Round tables + conversation front
Concept Mockup · Executive Dinner

Approximately 8–10 round tables with 7–8 guests each, targeting 60–80 total guests while preserving a front conversation area and clear sightlines. Final capacity depends on Sapphire Creek's approved floor plan.

Optional low 8′×12′ riser: planning allowance ≈ $1,250–$1,600. Current working assumption is floor-level unless testing the room shows a stage is necessary.

Branded Touchpoints

Subtle, premium branding inside the event

REAL should feel branded once guests arrive, but the Oak Room should still be the hero. The right level is one strong entrance moment, one polished touchpoint at every seat, a clean screen system, and restrained tabletop details — not giant banners everywhere.

01 · Arrival
Welcome Sign

One premium entrance sign at check-in or just outside the room. Black background, white type, high resolution, and minimal layout. Styled simply with a plant or candle so it feels intentional rather than promotional.

02 · At The Seat
Menus / Field Guides

Conference Casual can use a branded REAL field guide or notebook plus an agenda card. Executive Dinner can add a branded menu at each place setting, along with a simple conversation-prompt or schedule insert.

03 · Screen System
On-Screen Graphics

Use the Sapphire screen for a welcome slide, holding slide, interstitials, speaker intro slides, subtle sponsor recognition, and a clean closing slide. This is one of the cheapest ways to make the event feel intentionally produced.

04 · Details
Check-In + Tabletop

Keep the remaining branding restrained: name badges, table numbers, small prompt cards, VIP/sponsor identifiers, and one neat check-in setup. The goal is tactile brand presence without cluttering the room.

Working Print / Branding Package

Recommended pieces: 1 large welcome sign, 60–80 name badges, 60–80 field guides or notebooks, menus for the dinner option, table numbers, small prompt cards, check-in signage, VIP/sponsor identifiers, and a full screen-graphic package.

Ticketing Options

Choose the attendance model

Ticket pricing should support the business goal, not become the goal itself. Strategic complimentary seats remain available under any paid model.

Option A
Invite Only
$0

Best for: maximum control over who is in the room.

Tradeoff: highest no-show risk and no ticket offset.

Option B · Conference Casual
GA + VIP
$49 / $99

Why it works: low enough to keep the room accessible, high enough to create commitment.

Illustrative revenue: about $3.7K with 45 GA + 15 VIP tickets.

Option C · Executive Dinner
Dinner + VIP
$99 / $149

Why it works: the included seated dinner supports a materially higher ticket value.

Illustrative revenue: about $6.7K with 45 dinner + 15 VIP tickets.

Pricing is a working option, not a final recommendation. VIP should mean access — early entry, reserved seating, smaller speaker/Josh interaction, and priority Hot Seat or question submission — not simply a chair closer to the front.

Aggressive Marketing Strategy

Do not post it and hope

REAL should be invitation-led first and publicly marketed second. The goal is to create visible momentum before the broader launch, then use direct outreach, speaker and partner networks, organic content, email, and paid amplification together. The marketing should sell the value of the room — never read like a disguised recruiting campaign.

200+
Qualified Northeast Ohio agents / leaders in the working outreach pool

Build demand before we buy reach.

Start with a curated target list. Josh personally owns the highest-value relationships; leadership and the event team handle the broader list. We want the first registrations to come from people we deliberately wanted in the room, not strangers produced by an ad campaign.

01 · Direct
Personal Invitations

Identify a top 40–50 priority list. Josh personally reaches the highest-value names; leadership and recruiting support the remaining list through individual text, call, or email outreach.

02 · Social
Content Campaign

Approximately 3 feed posts and 2 short-form videos per week, supported by Stories. Lead with the speaker, uncomfortable questions, market realities, and clips that show what REAL will feel like.

03 · Email
Repeated Touches

Launch email, speaker reveal, value-led follow-up, social proof, urgency, and final reminders. Weekly initially; increase to roughly twice weekly in the final two weeks for non-registrants.

04 · Speakers
Borrowed Audience

Give every confirmed speaker a clean promo kit, unique registration link, suggested posts, and easy assets. Their audience should materially extend ours without turning the event into a speaker advertisement.

05 · Partners
Network Distribution

Sponsors receive seat inventory and a co-marketing toolkit. Prioritize partners with active Realtor relationships and ask them to invite specific agents, not simply blast a generic flyer.

06 · Paid
$750–$1K Amplification

Use paid social primarily to amplify the strongest speaker/value content and re-engage warm audiences. Paid spend supports the campaign; it should not be responsible for filling the room.

Phase 01 · Pre-Launch
Seed The Room

Target list · speaker teaser · direct invitations · sponsor outreach. Goal: secure 15–20 anchor commitments before broad public promotion.

Phase 02 · Launch
Create Proof

Open registration with real names already attached. Reveal headline value, speaker, venue, and limited ticket inventory. Publish the first wave of social and email simultaneously.

Phase 03 · Build
Stay Visible

Weekly direct outreach, speaker content, attendee proof, partner pushes, short-form video, and targeted paid amplification. Track every registration source.

Phase 04 · Final 14 Days
Close The Room

Personal follow-ups, remaining-seat messaging, two email touches per week, daily Stories, speaker reminders, and final targeted invitations to protect attendee quality.

Marketing Budget · ≈ $1,250

Working allowance for paid amplification, registration / promotional tools, and launch contingencies. Design and most content production remain in-house; professional event photography and videography are budgeted separately. This replaces the previous $300 marketing placeholder.

Registration Risk / Go-No-Go Plan

We do not spend $20K and wait to see who shows up

Attendance is treated as a managed risk with checkpoints before the largest variable costs are locked. “Confirmed” can include paid tickets and deliberate strategic comps, but it should not be padded with mass complimentary registrations simply to make the number look healthy.

Before Public Launch
15–20
Anchor commitments. If we cannot secure meaningful early interest from the people we specifically want, pause and revisit the speaker, offer, format, date, or price before pushing spend.
≈ 5 Weeks Out
30+
Minimum momentum. If below target, intensify personal outreach, speaker / partner promotion, and paid amplification. Do not assume organic registrations will rescue the event later.
≈ 3 Weeks Out
45+
Economics check. Review paid vs. comp mix, outside-TYT percentage, sponsor commitments, and remaining exposure before committing optional production or upgrades.
2 Weeks Out
50+
Final operating gate. Sapphire’s event materials require the final guest count two weeks prior. If registrations are materially below plan, deliberately resize the experience if contract terms allow — or postpone rather than stage an underfilled room.
Downside Protection

Before contracting, confirm Sapphire’s deposit, cancellation, minimum-spend, and reduction terms. Delay optional stage, upgraded furniture, excess printing, and other nonessential commitments until demand is proven. The objective is to expose The Young Team to a controlled feasibility cost first, then release the full event budget only as registrations justify it.

Sponsorship · $8K Target / $10K Stretch

Fewer, stronger partners

REAL should not become a vendor fair. The value is concentrated access to a curated room of real estate professionals, so the sponsorship model should favor a small number of relevant partners with meaningful seat inventory and tasteful recognition.

$4–5K
Presenting / Founding Partner

Premium recognition, category exclusivity, 4–6 reserved or VIP seats, inclusion in marketing, and networking access. No required speaking slot and no product demo.

$2–2.5K
Experience Partner

Could support hospitality, networking, Hot Seats, attendee materials, or another defined experience. Approximately 2–4 reserved seats.

$8–10K
Total Goal

Achievable through two or three strong partners rather than a wall of logos.

Potential categories: mortgage · title · insurance · real estate technology · home services · photography/media · other agent-facing businesses. Existing relationships, including Fello, can be considered as prospects based on fit and interest — not assumed as presenters or committed partners.

Timing Risk & Decision

Approve the strategy. Choose the execution.

An event at this level ideally has 10–12 weeks. REAL has about eight, so the concept phase needs to end quickly. The decision now is not a blind approval of a $20K+ event — it is whether to move into feasibility, choose the version we are pricing, and immediately test demand before the full budget is released.

Go / No-Go Checkpoint
By October 12

Confirm the correct December 1, 2026 venue date · receive final Sapphire cost structure and cancellation / deposit terms · determine headliner availability and preliminary fee · test sponsor interest · approve the budget ceiling · choose the ticket model · build the first 40–50-name priority invite list. If the core pieces are not viable, move the inaugural REAL to Q1 2027 rather than compromise the first experience.

Working Recommendation — Not Yet A Decision
Conference Casual · 60–80 · GA + VIP

This version protects networking, includes professional photo/video, keeps the likely Young Team investment below the executive-dinner version, and leaves room for tasteful branded touchpoints without overproducing the Oak Room. It should launch only after the first 15–20 anchor commitments demonstrate real demand. The deck intentionally leaves the final choice with leadership.
